title: CORS: what it is, when it breaks and how to fix it

videos.script:
The planner's page lives on port 5173, and its API on port 3000. {{ports}} To the browser, those are two strangers.

An origin is three things: the scheme, the host and the port. {{origin}} A page may send requests anywhere. It may only read the answers from its own origin, unless the other one says yes.

That yes is CORS. {{error}} You watch the browser refuse, and then notice something odd. The request still reached the server.

So CORS protects nothing on the server. {{wildcard}} It is a permission the server gives the browser, and the easy one, a star, is refused the moment cookies are involved.

You write the real fix, a list of one origin, and test it both ways. {{fix}} And then you see the best answer of all. Put the page and the API on one origin, and there is nothing to allow.
